_howToPublishANewCompanionBuild: THIS FILE IS THE ONLY PLACE YOU EDIT. No hand-computed hashes, no HTML edits.
1. Upload the new ZIP to  downloads/nerve/<version>-<channel>/  on GitHub.
Use a NEW folder every time. Never replace a file at a path already published.
2. Add an entry at the TOP of `releases` below: version, releaseDate, path,
status, and the 'improvements' lines you want shown on its card.
3. Leave the older entries alone. They stay downloadable so anyone still on the
matching extension can reinstall, and so old links keep working.
4. Commit.
On every deploy `npm run build` reads each ZIP and fills in the rest itself: the
SHA-256, the exact byte size, the human-readable size, the download URL, the
checksum URL and the filename, then writes the matching .sha256 sidecar next to
each ZIP. Because every hash is computed from the very bytes being served, a
published checksum can never drift from its published file.
THE ONE FIELD THAT MOVES ON RELEASE DAY is `forgeExtensionVersion`. Nerve's
extension and companion must be the SAME version, so that field — the version the
Forge listing actually delivers right now — decides what every card says:
version  = forgeExtensionVersion  ->  the Forge match. No warning.
version  > forgeExtensionVersion  ->  staged. Card says not to install it yet.
version  < forgeExtensionVersion  ->  rollback archive. Card says do not mix.
So while Forge still serves 0.67.1, that card reads 'Current Forge match' and the
0.68.7 card warns testers off. The moment Forge actually delivers 0.68.7, change
this one string and both cards relabel themselves and swap warnings. Do NOT move
it ahead of the Forge listing to make the site look current — the whole point is
that nobody installs a companion the extension cannot pair with.
status values: 'pending' | 'available'.
A download is rendered as a real, clickable control ONLY when its status is
'available' and its file actually exists. Otherwise it renders as a non-clickable
disabled control. The build REFUSES to publish and fails loudly if a ZIP named in
a release is missing, if the version string does not appear in its filename, or if
no listed release matches forgeExtensionVersion — that last guard stops anyone
deleting the older companion while the Forge listing still needs it. A failed
build leaves the previous deployment serving, so a mistake here cannot break the
live site.
_forgeExtensionVersion: The version the public Forge listing delivers TODAY — not the newest build we have.
Confirmed 15 September 2026: Forge is still on 0.67.1 while 0.68.7 is staged here.
Change it only when the Forge listing actually serves the new extension.

releases.headline: A substantial alpha update focused on safer live play, lower accidental AI usage, clearer setup, and more reliable Fantasy Grounds event handling.
improvements: Make native Fantasy Grounds bookkeeping changes without generating automatic AI cues. Deliberate Call Nerve requests stay available.
The extension and companion now require an exact version match, and say which of the two needs updating.
Table results and staged skill, ability-check and saving-throw messages settle into one follow-up instead of duplicate paid cues.

Attack and result stages settle together; completed native damage does not repeat or end the player's turn; remaining effect work stays available; and a final defeat preserves wounds, effects and roster entries until an explicit end-turn.
A confirmed current-room Story context can survive combat and a session resume without repinning.
Stale decisions are rejected without duplicate actions, and a claimed provider or listener failure is closed out cleanly rather than resubmitted as another possibly billed request.
Session and AI controls are easier to read, and the custom-app configuration launcher is now installed correctly.

releases.headline: The first publicly published companion, paired with the 0.67.1 Forge extension.

_installVerified: The listing is public and the extension is assigned to Live with Data installation,
but a signed-in acquisition plus a Fantasy Grounds updater installation has NOT been
run end to end yet. While this is false the site says so plainly and does not claim
Forge installation has been validated. Set it to true only once that test has actually
passed — it removes the caveat from the downloads and setup pages.

_comment: The public Fantasy Grounds thread for Nerve. Used for 'Discussion and bug reports'.
Anything posted there is public: the feedback page tells reporters to redact personal
information, credentials and private campaign material, and to keep support bundles
out of public posts. Email stays available for private reports.
Set formEnabled to true ONLY after RESEND_API_KEY, FEEDBACK_TO and FEEDBACK_FROM
are set in the Vercel project's environment variables, AND the privacy page has been
updated to say where form submissions are stored. While it is false the feedback page
hides the form entirely and offers the forum and email routes instead.

support.label: Support Nerve on Forge
_comment: Nerve support goes through the Forge listing's own donation/gift options. Do not add a
direct donation endpoint here and do not imply that donating is required or unlocks
anything. Buy Me a Coffee was removed from the Forge listing by the owner and is no
longer used for Nerve; any studio-wide support page is a separate matter.
